newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court cancels sell-off tender of steel maker.
newsitem.headline: Turk court cancels sell-off tender of steel maker.

text.p: An Ankara administrative court said on Tuesday it had cancelled the tender for the partial block sale of Eregli iron and steel plant, a centerpiece of Turkey's lethargic privatisation drive, because it was against the constitution.
"The tender lacked legal support as the constitutional court has already decided to cancel related articles of the privatisation law," the court said.
"Therefore it has been unanimously decided that the tender to privatise the company is cancelled," it said in its written verdict obtained by Reuters.
The government's Privatisation Administration held a tender in December 1996, to sell 30 to 40 percent of the giant steel maker through block sales and received bids from two companies in January.
The constitutional court cancelled in April parts of the privatisation law, saying that the articles on the assessment of the companies to be privatised were against the constitution.
Eregli, slated for privatisation in 1987, is Turkey's only flat steel producer and is one of the most important items of the government's privatisation programme, launched in 1986.
The government has gradually offered shares in the company on the Istanbul Stock Exchange since 1990. It currently holds 51.66 percent of the company, the rest being traded on the bourse.

Rumeli Holding, a Turkish conglomerate involved in cement making, banking and media business, and Zonguldak Yatirim, an enterprise of local investors of the Eregli town, had bid for the company in the tender in January.
A previous tender put out in 1995 to sell off the company was also cancelled in 1996 because the government said the company needed another assessment.
Eregli shares closed the day at 21,500 lira on Tuesday, up from 21,250 lira on Monday close.
